A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HALVA research, despite the changed title and method terminology. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original HALVA benchmark evaluations, ablations, HA-DPO retraining experiments, and qualitative outputs in Section 4 and Appendices B and D.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds VILA-based HALVA evaluations, POPE results, and further analyses and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: v1 explicitly describes word-level token aggregation, whereas v2 defines losses over multiword phrases such as 'white shirt'. Both retain the same loss structure and unspecified accumulation helper. The PDFs leave unclear whether phrase grouping changes the implemented procedure or clarifies the earlier description; renaming contrastive tuning to DPA alone is not a method change.

E1.justification: v2 adds POPE's object-existence evaluation, described as covering 500 images and 79 objects, in Appendix C.8. This extends coverage within the existing hallucination task family. Visual Genome training and the previously evaluated benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Comparison membership expands substantially: DoLA enters CHAIR; Woodpecker enters MME-Hall and AMBER; VCD, OPERA, LURE, RLHF-V, and GPT-4V enter MMHal-Bench; and HA-DPO, EOS, and additional RLHF methods enter HallusionBench. VILA supplies another evaluated base model. The HA-DPO data-transfer table also drops its untuned LLaVA row.

E3.justification: v2 adds a substantial model configuration: VILA-v1.5-13B with SigLIP, 384-pixel images, learning rate 2.5e-5, and loss weight 0.2. It also reports POPE evaluations with an alternative loss weight of 0.005 and adds zero-regularization controls. Existing LLaVA training budgets and main settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 extends the existing sensitivity plots with alpha=0 controls, adds a before/after alignment-loss distribution in Figure 5, and supplies additional chart and VILA case studies. POPE includes a limited loss-weight comparison. The existing data-sampling, reference-data, reference-model, and HA-DPO data-transfer ablations retain their results.

E5.justification: Both versions report three evaluations, averaged scores, and standard deviations for GPT-4-based evaluations. Additional result rows use the existing reporting practice; no changed repetition count, seed policy, confidence-interval procedure, or significance test is reported.

E6.justification: The original main LLaVA results are retained, but v2 adds extensive results for VILA, additional comparators, 13B general tasks, and POPE. Examples include VILA/HALVA AMBER F1 of 82.2/87.9 and default HALVA7B/13B POPE F1 of 84.8/84.9. POPE scores of 87.1/87.9 use alpha=0.005 and therefore represent different settings.

T1.justification: v2 introduces explicit multiword-span definitions and a formal DPA/DPO objective comparison while removing v1's three limiting-case statements about the contrastive loss. No theorem or proof is added. The new Appendix B expression includes an outer minus inconsistent with the objective minimized in Section 2.

C1.justification: The central claim of mitigating hallucination while preserving general capabilities remains. v2 sharpens the comparative novelty claim: localized phrase penalties, unlike sequence-level preference objectives, preserve capabilities through finer feedback. The abstract's newly highlighted numerical gains already appear in v1's AMBER results.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the mechanism discussion, attributing excessive divergence to sequence-level penalties and explaining the forward-KL choice. It also interprets Woodpecker's difficulty with short responses and adds an extended critique of POPE's restricted coverage and differing preferred loss weight. These are substantive additions beyond the retained divergence-based explanations.

D1.justification: v2 extends the existing implementation documentation with VILA hyperparameters, base-checkpoint access information, detailed training-data statistics, and complete generation examples. Appendix A corrects the KL calculation from raw logits to softmax probabilities. These refine reproducibility within the existing pipeline; the project's own code-release link remains a placeholder.

R1.justification: A dedicated new Appendix B positions DPA against DPO-derived hallucination methods through objectives and training-pair examples. Related work expands to RLAIF-V and other recent preference-alignment approaches, alongside VILA, SigLIP, DoLA, and additional references. This substantially develops the comparative positioning beyond v1's shorter discussion.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution paragraphs, and method exposition are substantially rewritten around DPA and phrase alignment. A dedicated comparison appendix is inserted, and qualitative material is organized by backbone. These changes substantially reshape the narrative despite retaining much experimental prose.

P2.justification: v2 merges v1 Figures 2 and 5, redraws and separates the augmentation and method diagrams, and adds a loss-distribution panel. Tables gain model groups and revised displays; Table 5 replaces its hard-accuracy column with Yes/No bias while retained HALVA hard-set results remain in the appendix. Prompt examples and qualitative figures are extensively reformatted and expanded.

improvement.justification: VILA evaluations strengthen portability evidence beyond v1's LLaVA-only experiments, and broader comparator coverage and POPE results better expose strengths and limits. Corrected KL pseudocode and worked generation examples improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by new inconsistencies, including Appendix B's loss sign and Table S8's LLaVA7B MME-Hall value of 684.3 versus 648.3 elsewhere.
